audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows disagree with the packet chart and with the mirror, which already set this matchup to Skill / Neeko / Neeko / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill. The page also grades it 'Favoured, difficulty 4/10' behind a 42.86% win rate, while its own late text says 'this is where the lane is lost'.
audit.why: Both layers agreed with each other and both disagreed with the mirror, so the two directions of this matchup currently render opposite answers on five rows.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the mirror's order as matched full/content pairs; diffRating 6/10, carryRating 7/10, tone to the even colour, both difficulty lines rewritten to 'Even matchup'.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] rendered Level 6 as a Neeko spike; Feast is 80/70/60s of true damage on a percentage of health and is by far the larger level-6 event.
audit.why: You still have a kill window at 6, but the row belongs to the champion who gains a flat execute on it.
audit.corrected: phases[4] and whys[4] rebuilt on Feast's 80s and its true damage; phases[5]/[6] rebuilt on the stacks and the resistance-proof late game.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields — whys[6], spikes[3], late and wants.foe[2] — say Feast goes through 'your shields' or 'shield and clone'. Neeko has no shield in her kit. spikes[1] says to ult 'while disguised/invisible'; her W is a clone with no invisibility. wants.foe[1] claims Rupture can 'interrupt your Pop Blossom channel'.
audit.why: The reason Feast is unanswerable is that it is TRUE damage on a percentage of health — resistances are the wrong purchase, which is a different and more useful lesson than a shield being pierced. And the ability that genuinely blanks a Neeko rotation is Feral Scream: a silence, in Riot's own text, on an 11-second cooldown at 300 range.
audit.corrected: Every shield reference replaced with the true-damage/resistances point; invisibility replaced with the disguise hiding Pop Blossom's preparation; report[5].t rebuilt on Feral Scream's silence; itemization now says to skip resistances.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d gave no number for Rupture and treated it as the whole green-light system.
audit.why: Rupture is a flat 6 seconds — it is not a window you can schedule a lane around. Feral Scream at 11s and Feast at 80s are the cooldowns that matter.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and phases[4].why.

edits.before: This is where the lane is lost and the 42.86% shows up. Cho's R is true-damage percent-HP — it ignores your Pop Blossom shield, your W clone, everything — and one cast deletes you regardless of your lead. You cannot 1v1 him; your job is to never be his R target. Group, ult clustered enemies in fights from fog, and let your team peel while you play the AoE-burst bomb, not a solo duelist.

notes: A phantom 'Pop Blossom shield' had spread to four fields here — Neeko has no shield anywhere in her kit, and the real reason Feast is unanswerable is that it is true damage on a percentage of health, which also means resistances are the wrong purchase. That correction now runs through whys[6], spikes[3], late, wants.foe[2] and the itemization line. Both layers agreed with each other while disagreeing with the mirror on five rows; I took the mirror's order, which is also the packet's. Per the mirror's explicit non-assertion I did NOT claim that a Rupture knock-up interrupts Pop Blossom's preparation — Riot's Rupture text describes a pop-up, damage and a slow with no grounding, so the derived grounding flag contradicts the description. wants.foe[1] now points at Feral Scream's silence, which Riot's text does support.
